items.definition:
a member of a British hereditary order of honour
He inherited the title of baronet from his father.

a black, sticky substance obtained from petroleum, used for making roads
The road was paved with asphalt, a mixture containing bitumen.

a light automatic rifle
The soldier carried a short-barreled carbine.

a pirate, especially one from the Barbary Coast; a pirate ship
The corsair sailed the Mediterranean, raiding merchant ships.

the eldest son of the King of France, and heir to the throne
The Dauphin of France was often a figure of political intrigue.

a physical blemish or distortion
The accident left him with a slight deformity in his leg.

a disorder in which an organ or tissue of the body wastes away
Muscular dystrophy is a group of diseases that cause progressive weakness and loss of muscle mass.

fluent or persuasive speaking or writing
His eloquence captivated the audience.

a phrase or statement written in memory of a person who has died, especially as an inscription on a tombstone
The epitaph on the tombstone read, 'Rest in Peace'.

waste matter discharged from the bowels or kidneys
The scientists analyzed the animal's excrement to study its diet.

a low and marshy or frequently flooded area of land
The rare birds nested in the remote fen.

an expression of good wishes to a person starting a journey or venture
We wished them godspeed on their long voyage.

the study of water on Earth
The course covers various aspects of hydrology, including river systems and groundwater.

a condition in which the body or a region of the body is deprived of adequate oxygen supply
Symptoms of severe hypoxia include confusion and cyanosis.

a rank below black belt in martial arts
He achieved his first kyu rank in judo.

a dark brown or black pigment occurring in the hair, skin, and iris of the eye
Melanin protects the skin from UV radiation.

a hormone involved in social bonding
Oxytocin is often called the "love hormone."

a quality that evokes pity or sadness
The film's ending was full of pathos, bringing tears to many eyes.

the quality of being physical
The dancer's performance was marked by incredible physicality.

the art of making portraits
Her exhibition showcased a wide range of portraiture styles.

a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought
The school's guiding precepts emphasized respect and integrity.

the quality of being strong and healthy; the ability to withstand adverse conditions
The robustness of the system was tested under extreme conditions.

the four-dimensional continuum of space and time
Einstein's theory of relativity describes the fabric of spacetime.

a broad strip or area of something
The combine harvester cut a wide swath through the wheat field.

a junction between two nerve cells
Information is transmitted across the synapse.

ringing or buzzing in the ears
He suffers from chronic tinnitus.

a cause of great trouble or suffering
They faced many tribulations during their journey.

the power of using one's will
He acted entirely of his own volition.

an unfortunate or unhappy person
The poor wretch had lost everything.

A person who applies to a higher court for a reversal of the decision of a lower court.
The appellant filed a notice of appeal within the deadline.

A workshop or studio, especially one used by an artist or designer.
The fashion designer worked late into the night in her atelier.

Sulfur, especially in its traditional association with hell.
The preacher spoke of fire and brimstone.

A device in an internal combustion engine for mixing air with a fine spray of liquid fuel.
He had to clean the carburetor to get the old engine running.

An underground cemetery, especially one consisting of tunnels and rooms with recesses for coffins or tombs.
They explored the ancient catacombs beneath the city.

A common sexually transmitted infection.
Chlamydia is a bacterial infection that can affect both men and women.

(In polygamous societies) a woman who lives with a man but has lower status than his wife or wives.
In ancient times, kings often had concubines in addition to their wives.

a feeling of disappointment resulting from the discovery that something is not as good as one believed it to be
He felt a deep sense of disillusionment after the election results.

a geological epoch that lasted from about 56 to 33.9 million years ago
Many early mammal fossils are found from the Eocene epoch.

liveliness of mind or spirit; wit
The team showed great esprit and determination.

the scientific description of peoples and cultures with their customs, habits, and mutual differences
Her research involved extensive ethnography of the local community.

a man who has been castrated, especially (in the past) one employed to guard the women's living areas at an oriental court
In ancient times, eunuchs often served in royal courts.

a rapid, irregular, and unsynchronized contraction of muscle fibers
Atrial fibrillation is a common type of irregular heartbeat.

The study of the influence of geography on politics and international relations.
The analyst discussed the geopolitics of the Middle East.

The study of historical writing.
The course covered the historiography of the American Civil War.

The process of interbreeding individuals from genetically distinct populations to produce a hybrid.
Plant breeders use hybridization to create new varieties of crops.

The worship of idols; extreme admiration, love, or reverence for something or someone.
The ancient civilization practiced idolatry, worshipping many gods.

Cinema; film
The director's latest work is a masterpiece of independent kino.

A British nobleman ranking below a duke and above an earl
The marquess inherited the vast estate from his father.

a strong and sudden flow or emission
There was an outpouring of grief after the tragedy.

a type of falcon known for its speed
The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in the world.

the attribution of a personal nature or human characteristics to something non-human
Justice is often depicted as a blindfolded woman, a classic personification.

a chemical substance produced and released into the environment by an animal, affecting the behavior of others of its species
Insects use pheromones to communicate with each other.

a tendency to suffer from a particular condition or to behave in a particular way
He has a genetic predisposition to heart disease.

insurance that an insurance company buys from another insurance company
The company uses reinsurance to spread its risk.

a sacred place; a private place where one is not to be disturbed
His study was his private sanctum, where he could work undisturbed.

the enjoyment, expression, or pursuit of physical, especially sexual, pleasure
The painting captured the sensuality of the human form.

a diversion or a bypass; a medical device to drain fluid
The surgeon inserted a shunt to relieve the pressure.

a tubular support placed temporarily inside a blood vessel or other duct
The doctor inserted a stent to keep the artery open.

an underlying and often unspoken meaning or message
The subtext of their conversation was that they were unhappy.

the state of being sure or certain; a person who takes responsibility for another's performance
He acted as surety for his brother's loan.

a system of government that is centralized and dictatorial
The rise of totalitarianism in the 20th century led to widespread conflict.

a subordinate official, especially in a government department
The undersecretary presented the new policy to the committee.

a true principle or belief, especially one of fundamental importance
The verity of his statement was undeniable.

the action of singling someone out for cruel or unjust treatment
The report highlighted the ongoing victimization of minority groups.
